title: Skip storage blocks that cannot contain the customer
goal: Use min/max statistics and physical layout to avoid reading files or micro-partitions that cannot match a filter.
tag: Focused certification lesson · query pruning and performance · cycle 4, position 2
concept:
A warehouse labels each box with the smallest and largest customer ID inside. An order for customer 42 does not require opening a box labeled 1–20.

Databricks records statistics for data files. Snowflake records metadata for micro-partitions. At query time, each engine can prune—skip—storage blocks whose ranges cannot match the filter. Better physical grouping creates tighter ranges and more skipping.
example: Six blocks hold customer ranges 1–20, 21–40, 41–60, and so on. Filtering for customer 42 scans only block 3. If every block overlaps 1–120, all six remain candidates even though only one contains the row.

use_case.when: Use pruning evidence when a large table is slow even though queries filter on a selective customer, date, tenant, or region column.
use_case.example: A 20-TB order table is usually queried by tenant and event date, but each query still scans most files.
use_case.decision: First confirm the filter is eligible and statistics exist. Improve layout only when repeated workload evidence justifies the write, maintenance, and service cost; do not cluster every column.

practice: Move the overlap control. Predict how many of six blocks remain candidates for customer 42 before reading the scan count.
boundary: The local model uses six equal synthetic ranges and one equality predicate. It does not execute either engine, measure bytes or cost, model nulls, expressions, joins, cached results, dynamic file pruning, semi-structured data, or optimizer decisions. Vendor SQL was not run.

product_sections.title: Databricks: file statistics make data skipping possible
product_sections.html:
Each file carries a small map. Delta statistics can include minimum, maximum, null count, and record count. A filter can skip a file only when statistics prove it cannot match. Unity Catalog managed tables with predictive optimization can collect statistics beyond the first 32 schema columns based on workload.

-- sourced SQL sketch; not executedALTER TABLE ops.orders SET TBLPROPERTIES (  'delta.dataSkippingStatsColumns'='customer_id,event_date');ANALYZE TABLE ops.orders COMPUTE DELTA STATISTICS;

Failure/fix. Statistics on the wrong columns or heavily overlapping files reduce skipping. Choose liquid-clustering keys from recurring filters and measure benefit. Predictive optimization applies to Unity Catalog managed tables and has prerequisites; external tables have different defaults.

Execution label. SQL is an unexecuted vendor sketch. The file map is local JavaScript.
product_sections.markdown: Delta file min/max statistics let the engine skip impossible files. Collect statistics for recurring filter columns; use liquid clustering only when workload evidence supports its maintenance cost. SQL was not run.

product_sections.title: Snowflake: micro-partition metadata drives pruning
product_sections.html:
Micro-partitioning is automatic. Snowflake stores range and distinct-value metadata for micro-partitions. Query pruning uses that metadata. Overlapping ranges increase clustering depth; a smaller average depth is better clustered for the chosen columns.

-- sourced SQL sketch; not executedSELECT SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION(  'OPS.ORDERS', '(CUSTOMER_ID)');ALTER TABLE OPS.ORDERS CLUSTER BY (CUSTOMER_ID);

Failure/fix. A clustering key can improve a large table with selective, repeated filters, but Automatic Clustering consumes serverless resources. Inspect pruning and clustering information before paying to maintain a key.

Execution label. No Snowflake SQL ran. The depth-to-candidate view is a local model.
product_sections.markdown: Snowflake creates micro-partitions automatically and prunes with their metadata. High overlap depth is evidence of weak clustering for a filter. Clustering can cost serverless credits; measure first. SQL was not run.

title: One barrier timeout breaks the gate for every waiter
goal: Handle CyclicBarrier's all-or-none breakage instead of assuming the remaining workers can continue normally.
concept:
Three runners must reach a starting gate before anyone begins lap two. If runner 3 never arrives, runner 1 eventually leaves. The gate is now broken for runner 2 as well.

Java's CyclicBarrier coordinates a fixed number of parties. If one waiter times out or is interrupted, the barrier enters a broken state and the other waiters receive BrokenBarrierException. Recovery needs a coordinated new phase, often a new barrier.
example: Shard workers A and B finish phase 1. Worker C is stuck. A's 100-ms wait expires. B does not proceed with a partial result; its wait fails because the same barrier is broken.

use_case.when: Use a barrier when a fixed set of peers must finish each repeated phase before any enters the next phase.
use_case.example: Three in-memory simulation shards exchange boundary values after every iteration.
use_case.decision: Use CountDownLatch for a one-time completion signal, Phaser when parties change dynamically, or an external durable coordinator for distributed jobs. Never use an in-process barrier across machines.

practice: Toggle whether worker C arrives. Watch all three pass together or the timeout break the phase for everyone.
boundary: The recorded Java example uses two waiting threads, one missing party, and a timeout. It does not prove scheduling order, fairness, distributed coordination, recovery correctness, interruption policy, or production timeout values.

';};thirdArrives.onchange=paintBarrier;paintBarrier();

title: A game day needs a measurable hypothesis and a stop condition
goal: Design resilience experiments that test one claim while automatically limiting unexpected customer impact.
concept:
Do not pull a fire alarm just to see what happens. State what should remain safe, choose the fault, and define the reading that stops the exercise.

A useful game day begins from a measured steady state, forms a hypothesis, injects a bounded fault, watches customer-visible metrics, and stops when a guardrail crosses its threshold. The result is evidence for the architecture and the team's response—not theater.
example: Hypothesis: removing 20% of EKS workers keeps order success at or above 99%. Stop the experiment if five-minute success falls below 98%. At 98.6%, continue and observe recovery. At 97.8%, stop and restore capacity.

use_case.when: Run a game day after non-production resilience tests pass and before relying on a failover, autoscaling, or degraded-mode claim in production.
use_case.example: Verify that one EKS node-group impairment preserves order processing and pages the right team within three minutes.
use_case.decision: Use a tabletop exercise first when production fault injection is unsafe or the human procedure is the main uncertainty. Start narrow, obtain authorization, exclude critical periods, and automate stop conditions.

practice: Change observed success rate. Watch the hypothesis remain supported or the stop condition terminate the experiment.
boundary: This arithmetic model does not inject faults, call AWS FIS, measure a workload, authorize production risk, choose thresholds, restore capacity, or prove resilience. A real experiment requires change controls, owners, observability, rollback, and persisted evidence.

title: Two agent turns need one owner of session history
goal: Coordinate concurrent writers so each agent turn sees the history that its final ordering claims it saw.
concept:
A shared notebook can contain both Alice's and Bob's notes while still telling the wrong story if both wrote answers from the same earlier page.

An agent session stores conversation history. The OpenAI Agents SDK serializes reads and mutations through one OpenAI Conversations session instance. Separate instances or external writers still need application-level coordination. Serialize whole turns per session ID when order matters.
example: Turns A and B both read history version 8. A answers and appends version 9. B then appends an answer generated without A, even though the final ledger places B after A. With a per-session queue, B reads version 10 and its answer matches the visible order.

use_case.when: Coordinate by session ID when web requests, workers, retries, or channels can start overlapping turns for the same conversation.
use_case.example: A user submits a chat message from the web while a webhook starts another run against the same support session.
use_case.decision: Allow parallel runs for independent session IDs. For one ordered conversation, use one queue/lock and an idempotent request ID; do not rely on one storage method's internal lock to serialize an entire model-tool turn.

practice: Toggle serialized turns. Watch the version each turn reads and compare it with the final ledger order.
boundary: The browser models ordered history versions, not the Agents SDK, a model, network retries, Redis/SQLite transactions, RunState recovery, idempotency, or distributed locks. The Python replay is synthetic and local.

title: Short waves merge until the whole material oscillates together
goal: Understand the reported wave-coarsening path from local vibrations to a globally synchronized time-crystalline state.
concept:
Small ripples on a sheet can merge into fewer, longer ripples. In this active material, the vibration's wavelength, period, and amplitude grew together over time.

Researchers observed this wave coarsening in one- and two-dimensional mechatronic metamaterials with non-reciprocal interactions. The process ended in a system-spanning synchronized oscillation described as a time crystal. Adding friction arrested coarsening and exposed persistent edge-localized waves.
example: A teaching trace starts with eight short wave domains. Successive merge steps leave four, then two, then one system-spanning mode. Turning on friction arrests the toy trace at two domains. This illustrates the paper's reported direction, not its equations or measured scaling.

use_case.when: Use this research to reason about controllable collective vibration in active materials, acoustics, optomechanics, living matter, or soft-robotics research.
use_case.example: A research team wants mechanical units to synchronize into a large-scale oscillation without a central clock.
use_case.decision: Treat it as foundational laboratory research. It suggests an organizing principle, not a production-ready soft-robotics control system; device lifetime, energy, stability, scale, and control remain open engineering questions.

practice: Move the coarsening step and toggle friction. Watch domain count and wavelength change together, or arrest before one global mode forms.
boundary: This discrete animation is an original teaching analogy. It does not solve the paper's nonlinear equations, reproduce dynamical scaling, model non-reciprocal forces, energy, noise, topology, friction, geometry, or validate a time crystal. Claims are limited to the reported experiments and simulations.

title: A low-trust workflow may read the cache; do not let it rewrite the cache
goal: Use GitHub Actions cache-mode so untrusted events cannot poison cache contents later restored by privileged jobs.
concept:
A visitor may borrow a shared toolbox. That does not mean the visitor should replace the tools before the owner uses it.

GitHub caches are restored as-is and are not signed. Low-trust triggers that resolve to the default branch receive read-only cache access by default. Explicit cache-mode: write overrides that protection and can let untrusted code plant files that a later privileged workflow executes.
example: A pull_request_target job restores the default branch's dependency cache. With effective mode read, a save is skipped and the job continues. If the workflow forces write after checking out fork code, the fork can replace cached build tooling for the next trusted deployment.

use_case.when: Set cache access explicitly when workflows run from fork-controlled or otherwise low-trust events, especially reusable workflows and jobs that later handle secrets.
use_case.example: A fork PR runs tests using a default-branch Maven cache while only a push-to-main workflow refreshes that cache.
use_case.decision: Prefer read-only restore for low-trust jobs and trusted push jobs for writes. Never put secrets in caches. If correctness depends on the cache, the build is already broken—cache miss must remain safe.

practice: Switch event trust and explicit mode. Watch restore/save permissions and the cache-poisoning path.
boundary: The model simplifies GitHub's event classification and cache scopes. It does not run Actions, inspect a repository, prove an action is safe, model merge-ref scope, reusable-workflow ceilings, cache eviction, signed artifacts, secrets, or every trigger.

title: Binary Protobuf preserves unknown fields; a JSON hop can erase them
goal: Evolve messages without silently deleting new fields when an older intermediary forwards them.
concept:
An old postal sorter may not understand a new sticker, but it can leave the sticker on the package. If it rewrites the address onto a fresh plain box, the unknown sticker disappears.

An older proto3 parser keeps well-formed unknown binary fields and includes them when serializing again. Converting the message to ProtoJSON, or copying fields one by one into a new message, can lose unknown fields.
example: New producer sends order_id=42 as field 1 and priority=EXPRESS as new field 7. An old binary proxy understands field 1 but preserves field 7 during binary parse and reserialize. A binary → JSON → binary proxy drops field 7 because ProtoJSON generally does not propagate unknown fields.

use_case.when: Protect unknown fields when old services, queues, gateways, or storage layers must forward newer Protobuf messages during a rolling upgrade.
use_case.example: A v1 Kafka enrichment service reads a v2 order event and republishes it before every consumer has upgraded.
use_case.decision: Keep opaque binary forwarding or use message CopyFrom/MergeFrom when preservation matters. Use JSON at human-facing boundaries only after accepting its different evolution behavior, and reserve deleted field numbers and names.

practice: Choose binary forwarding or a JSON hop. Watch field 7 survive or disappear while field 1 remains.
boundary: The local dictionary model is not a Protobuf encoder. It omits wire types, generated APIs, editions, enum behavior, maps, oneofs, extensions, deterministic serialization, malformed data, language differences, and schema registries.

walkthrough.limit: The local dictionary model is not a Protobuf encoder. It omits wire types, generated APIs, editions, enum behavior, maps, oneofs, extensions, deterministic serialization, malformed data, language differences, and schema registries.

sources: Protocol Buffers proto3 language guide: unknown fields
visual_explanation: The same field-numbered package travels through two paths. Binary forwarding keeps the unknown sticker; the JSON path visibly emits only fields the old schema knows.
written_questions: Which services deserialize and reconstruct Protobuf messages field by field today?
Where is a JSON conversion acceptable, and where must unknown binary fields survive?
